description: A tech lead must approve the initial production rollout policy for a new authorization-cache path, setting the rollout size, cache lifetime, invalidation behavior, and customer handling after the normal preflight review.

shared_context.S1: The new authorization-cache path passed its planned unit, integration, and staging tests.
shared_context.S2: The production feature flag is scheduled for its first customer traffic on Monday morning.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final authority over the rollout policy and its required operating safeguards.
shared_context.S4: The team's standard preflight practice is for backend engineering, site reliability, and customer support to report any relevant operational constraints before Riley finalizes the flag settings.

PF1.text: While tracing a separate permissions bug yesterday, Mina found that 23 legacy admin endpoints update permissions without emitting the invalidation event consumed by the new cache; she has not yet filed the adapter work because she was confirming which endpoints still use that path.

PF2.text: Owen's load rehearsal this morning measured invalidation-queue propagation at a 9-minute p95 and showed that the queue remains within its safe operating limit only when the first rollout cohort is capped at 10 percent; he has not updated the rollout ticket because the rehearsal finished after the change-control review began.

PF3.text: Tessa confirmed during a support-case review that all 11 SCIM-managed enterprise accounts use an admin workflow that cannot yet explain delayed permission changes, so those accounts must be excluded from the first rollout and a support playbook must be prepared before they are enabled; she has not posted the finding because the cases were being reassigned between support queues.

acceptance_conditions: The initial rollout must be capped at exactly 10 percent.
The authorization cache TTL must be exactly 300 seconds.
The legacy permission-update path must have its invalidation adapter enabled before rollout.
The revocation kill switch must be enabled.
SCIM-managed enterprise accounts must be excluded from the first rollout.
A support playbook commitment for SCIM-managed enterprise accounts must be recorded.
A legacy invalidation adapter commitment covering the 23 endpoints must be recorded.
Mina's discovery about the 23 legacy endpoints must be spoken aloud and cited by Riley as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The passing tests do not expose the 23 legacy endpoints, and PF1 changes the plan from ordinary cache enablement to enabling and committing to a legacy invalidation adapter.

PF2 changes the initial cohort to exactly 10 percent, the cache lifetime to exactly 300 seconds, and the operating plan to require an enabled revocation kill switch because propagation reaches a 9-minute p95.
PF3 changes the first-rollout customer assignment to exclude SCIM-managed enterprise accounts and adds the required support-playbook commitment for those 11 accounts.
